data.name: Adelpho
data.gender_notes: Adelpho is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek word 'adelphos' meaning 'brother'. In the New Testament, the term 'adelphoi' is used to refer to fellow Christians, indicating a strong bond of faith and brotherhood. The name Adelpho carries the meaning “Brother, Kin” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Adelpho usually hope their child will grow to embody brother, kin and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adelpho total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: אדלפו
in_hebrew.meaning: אח או אחי, משמעות שם adelphos
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אדלפו נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'אדלפוס' (adelphos), שפירושה אח או אחי. הוא משמש לתיאור קשרי אחווה וחיבה בין אחים, וגם משמש כמטפורה לקשרים רוחניים בין מאמינים. השם מופיע בברית החדשה ומשמש כביטוי לאחווה נוצרית.

in_greek.name: Αδελφο
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αδελφο προέρχεται από το ελληνικό 'αδελφός' (adelphos), που σημαίνει αδελφός ή αδελφή. Ο όρος χρησιμοποιείται στην Καινή Διαθήκη για να περιγράψει τις σχέσεις μεταξύ των πιστών στην πρώτη Εκκλησία, τονίζοντας την αδελφότητα και την αγάπη μεταξύ των μελών της κοινότητας των πιστών.

in_latin.name: Adelpho
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Adelpho derivatur a voce Graeca 'adelphos', quae significat fratrem vel germanum. In Ecclesia primitiva, hoc nomen ad significandam fraternitatem et caritatem inter fideles usurpabatur, reflectens vinculum spirituale inter credentes.

in_english.name: Adelpho
in_english.meaning: Means brother, sibling or fraternal love

It is rooted in New Testament Greek and used to express brotherly love and unity among Christians. Historically, it signifies the bond of brotherhood in faith and has been adopted in various Christian traditions to symbolize spiritual kinship and fraternity.
